thread:
anika: quick heads-up — ran onboarding eval for caelum-embed-v1 (int8 per-channel) against short-query-100k. recall@1 down ~18% vs opal-v2 baseline :confused:

matt: ouch. numbers? recall@5?

anika: recall@1 0.52 (baseline 0.70), recall@5 0.78 (baseline 0.86). silhouette score dropped from 0.21 -> 0.12.

samira: did you use L2-normalization before indexing? int8 can skew norms.

anika: used same pipeline we use for float models (normalize then index). suspect quantization clamp on tail dims.
jordan: can you paste a few nearest-neighbor examples and distances?
anika: sure — sample query "how to reset my password" -> expected: "password reset steps", "account recovery". actual top1 is "change email settings" distance 0.37, top2 is correct but distance 0.45. baseline top1 dist 0.11. snippet:
```
query: "how to reset my password"
caelum-int8 top3: [("change email settings", 0.37), ("password reset steps", 0.45), ("account recovery", 0.48)]
opal-v2 top3: [("password reset steps", 0.11), ("account recovery", 0.12), ("two-factor reset", 0.18)]
```

matt: those distance shifts look like per-dim scale issues. do we have per-channel scales logged from the quant job?

ci-eval-bot: eval job 13579 completed: https://ci.redwood.ai/evals/13579 — metrics: recall@1=0.52, recall@5=0.78, silhouette=0.12. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/13579/ (embeddings, nearest-neighbors).

samira: can we re-run with float L2-normalize after dequant (i.e. cast back to float32 before normalizing) to confirm if normalization order matters?
jordan: also try per-channel vs per-tensor quantization, and run a run with symmetric quantization disabled. small change but sometimes fixes high-dim leakage.
anika: kicking off CI job to compare 4 variants: (1) original int8 (per-channel), (2) int8 per-tensor, (3) int8 per-channel + post-dequant norm, (4) float32 baseline. command I'm using:
```bash
python infra/evals/run_embed_eval.py --model caelum-embed-v1 --dataset short-query-100k --k 1,5 --variants per_channel,per_tensor,post_dequant,fp32 --save-artifacts
```

matt: include a whitening/pca variant too — sometimes quant moves variance to subspace that PCA fixes.
samira: +1 on PCA. also run small-batch vs large-batch infer to rule out accumulation/precision differences.
anika: added pca variant and batch-size sweep. job ids: 13580 (per-tensor), 13581 (post-dequant), 13582 (pca), 13583 (batch-sweep). linking dashboards as they finish.

ci-eval-bot: job 13581 finished: recall@1=0.63, recall@5=0.81, silhouette=0.16. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/13581/

matt: interesting — post-dequant norm recovered ~11 points on R@1. that implies normalization order is the culprit.
jordan: do we have a quick patch to make our pipeline normalize after casting to float at inference time? shouldn't be large perf hit.
samira: can also try doing per-sample L2 scaling at index time (store normalized vectors) as a safe workaround.
anika: agreed. for immediate rollbacks: (A) switch indexing pipeline to force post-dequant L2 norm, (B) flag model as degraded in console so production routes to opal-v2 for short-query route.
matt: +1 on flagging routes. any showstopper for deployment?
anika: nothing urgent — throughput tests are fine. it's purely quality regression on short queries. I'll open a release-blocking flag and a PR with the normalization fix.

jordan: ping me on the PR. also add a small unit eval (1000 short queries) in CI to catch this for future quant bringups.
samira: can we add a metric to detect "norm-drift" (mean L2 of embeddings vs baseline) so future quant jobs fail fast?
matt: yes, add mean L2 and std L2 deltas to eval report and threshold the delta.
anika: creating ticket TRACK-2391 for norm-drift alert + PR for post-dequant-norm.

ci-eval-bot: TRACK-2391 created by anika.

anika: thanks all — will update here when PR merges / routes changed :white_check_mark: :eyes:

matt: nice triage. :thumbsup:
